source.title: Steering Externalities: Benign Activation Steering Unintentionally Increases Jailbreak Risk for Large Language Models
source.authors: Chen Xiong; Zhi-Yuan He; Pin-Yu Chen; Ching-Yun Ko; Tsung-Yi Ho

page_placements.theme: Runtime instructions, demonstrations and steering modulate safety

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether benign, inference-time activation steering changes harmful-request safety and jailbreak success, extending the related safety-degradation claim to a different intervention from fine-tuning.
record.gate_note: The study does not fine-tune models or compare aligned models with base models. It does measure harmful-request outcomes under benign activation steering, adaptive jailbreaks, and per-token KL shifts. Utility-only checks, qualitative examples, and cited results from prior work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: Harmful-request ASR and refusal rates are measured under benign activation steering, which the authors show mainly shifts the opening tokens away from refusal. This is a new opening-bypass route for V4. The KL analysis compares original and steered models, not aligned and base models, so it does not test V3.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that benign compliance or JSON activation steering weakens refusal, raises intrinsic harmful ASR and amplifies black-box jailbreaks. They attribute this to early-token shifts away from refusal prefixes, explicitly citing the shallow safety alignment hypothesis, plus representation shifts. They recommend red-teaming steered models and report preliminary mitigation with STEER-BIND. Their 'up to 99% ASR' headline is not matched by any reported table; the maximum is 94.25%.
record.recipe_differences: Inference-time activation vectors derived from benign contrastive or instruction-format data; no model fine-tuning. The paper also tests black-box CoP, PAIR, and TAP jailbreaks.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by model, steering type (compliance generally has larger effects than JSON), attack condition, and refusal judge. JSON refusal-rate decreases are smaller than compliance decreases in the reported SorryBench results.

fits_no_version.finding: Per-token KL between the original and benign-steered models peaks in the first few response tokens on harmful prompts, then stabilizes (figures only).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign activation steering perturbs output distributions mainly at the first response positions.

fits_no_version.finding: Steered harmful-prompt representations cross an illustrative t-SNE harmful/harmless boundary (60.8% compliance, 58.2% JSON).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign activation steering shifts harmful-prompt representations toward harmless-like regions.

fits_no_version.finding: STEER-BIND (mixed benign-compliance and harmful-refusal vector) cuts ASR relative to compliance steering (36→5%, CoP 93→76%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety-aware steering-vector construction attenuates steering externalities.

record.problems: No error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests are stated. Main evaluations use three models, and the additional-model experiments use 50 HarmBench questions. Refusal results rely on model-based judges. The authors describe the t-SNE boundary analysis as illustrative. The text reports the KL pattern graphically without numerical KL values. Table 8's value-column label says compliance although its heading and accompanying text identify JSON steering.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row cap. Utility-only outcomes (Table 1, Table 6, Figure 5), qualitative jailbreak examples, cited prior-study results, and layer-selection details were excluded because they do not report separate measured outcomes of the claim versions.

untested.parts: Benign data builds steering vectors; no benign fine-tuning.
No aligned-vs-base per-token KL; only original-vs-steered KL.
Prefilling, adversarial suffixes and decoding changes are not tested as isolated interventions.
No test of what causes the shallowness.
STEER-BIND is a steering-vector construction, not deep alignment training; no token-depth robustness test.

missing.what: Steering-coefficient ablation (alpha 0–2.0) of harmful SorryBench refusal rate on Llama-3-8B-Instruct: a dose-response of refusal loss, wrongly excluded as utility-only.
Original-model ASR in Table 5 (4% benchmark-only, 73% under CoP), which differs from Table 10 for the same model.

record.verdict_notes: Linking to V4 treats activation steering as a route past the refusal opening. The compliance vector is built from refusal- vs compliance-prefixed continuations, and the authors show first-token changes, but it is not prefilling, suffixes or decoding changes. A reviewer may prefer to treat all ASR rows as a separate steering-externality claim. Not an original source. No uncertainty estimates are given; most refusal results use 100 prompts. Additional-model results use 50 prompts.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples or few-shot-to-hundreds-example sweep.
Benign datasets are used to derive activation-steering vectors, not to fine-tune the models; ordinary or carefully chosen benign fine-tuning is not tested.
Measures per-token KL between original aligned and benign-steered models, not between aligned and base models.
Tests benign steering and black-box jailbreak attacks, not compliant-prefix prefill, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes as isolated interventions.
No localization or ablation of safety-carrying weights or ranks.
Does not test whether safety-training data or objective causes safety to be shallow.
STEER-BIND is a safety-aware steering-vector construction, not training to spread safety beyond initial tokens; no test of token-depth robustness.

relation.reason: The study measures safety degradation under steering and amplification of jailbreak attacks, with early-token analyses bearing on the proposed refusal-bypass mechanism.

tranche.reason: Inference-time benign activation steering supplies a new setting with harmful-completion and refusal measurements bearing on V4.

source_check.notes: Table 5 and Table 10 give inconsistent original/compliance ASRs for Llama-3; retain their results separately. The KL comparison is original aligned versus steered, so it does not directly test V3's aligned-versus-base claim.
